主要内容: Fourteen states, including Louisiana and Wyoming, have filed lawsuits against the Biden administration over its moratorium on new oil and natural gas leases on public lands and waters. The moratorium, which was implemented on January 27, 2021, is part of a series of executive actions aimed at addressing climate change and reducing carbon emissions. The states, all led by Republican attorneys general, argue that the moratorium will negatively impact communities reliant on oil and gas drilling and increase energy prices. The Louisiana lawsuit specifically requested the Bureau of Land Management to restart quarterly oil and gas lease sales. The Interior Department has not commented on the lawsuits. While the moratorium does not end fossil fuel extraction, as the industry still holds undeveloped leases, drilling on federal lands contributes to about a quarter of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions and generates billions in revenue.
